what_it_is.value: Agent multiplexer CLI (npm `dmux`) that runs on tmux: a 40-column Ink/React control sidebar in one tmux pane manages a grid of tmux panes, each with its own git worktree, branch and coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, etc.). It tracks per-pane agent status and attention, offers a read-only file-browser pane (code or diff preview), merge and PR flows, lifecycle hooks and durable terminals that resume agent sessions. It puts no graphical content in the terminal; an earlier HTTP API, Vue web dashboard and tunnel/QR remote were removed on 2026-02-20.
what_it_is.note: [measured] README, docs/src/content/core-concepts.js, and commit 75cd109 ('refactor: remove server-side API and related infrastructure', deleted src/server/*, TunnelService, remotePopup) read via gh api 2026-09-24.

language.value: TypeScript on Node >=18 (Ink 5 + React 18 TUI), with a Vue 3 frontend directory and a small Swift macOS notification helper. GitHub bytes: HTML 4.98 MB (coverage/docs artifacts), TypeScript 2.27 MB, JavaScript 0.37 MB, Vue 64 KB, CSS 43 KB, Swift 28 KB, Shell 11 KB.
language.note: [measured] languages API plus package.json dependencies (ink ^5.0.1, react ^18.2.0, vue ^3.5.22). HTML tops the byte count only because committed coverage/ and docs/ pages are counted.

graphics_mechanism.value: none — text cells only. The sidebar and every dialog are Ink renderers; each dialog is a separate Node process launched inside `tmux display-popup -E` that returns its result through a temp JSON file (src/utils/popup.ts). The file browser syntax-highlights text with cli-highlight and refuses binaries ('Binary file preview is disabled. Open the file externally if needed.', src/utils/fileBrowser.ts:710). No Sixel, Kitty or iTerm2 image handling anywhere in src/.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] read src/utils/popup.ts (display-popup -E -w -h -d -b -s border-fg, -x C -y C), src/utils/fileBrowser.ts, context/POPUPS.md ('Each popup must be a separate Node process (tmux limitation)').

where_it_draws.value: split panes + floating panel. tmux tiled layout with a fixed 40-column sidebar on the left and agent panes in a computed grid (default max pane width 80, min 50 columns, columns before rows, orphan panes span full height, debounced relayout on resize). The file browser opens as another tmux pane tied to the source worktree's project group. Menus and dialogs are modal tmux display-popups, centered or offset past the sidebar; Alt+Shift+M positions the pane menu over the focused pane. Attention shows as `![ready]` in the tmux pane-border-format and in the sidebar. Pane content scrolls as ordinary tmux text; popups sit above everything and do not scroll.
where_it_draws.note: [measured] context/LAYOUT.md (layout phases), src/constants/layout.ts (DEFAULT_MAX_PANE_WIDTH = 80, DEFAULT_MIN_PANE_WIDTH = 50), src/index.ts:1304-1305 (pane-border-status top, pane-border-format with @dmux_attention), docs keyboard-shortcuts.js (Alt+Shift+M).

input_model.value: tmux owns focus: j/Enter switches tmux focus to a pane and agents receive keys straight from tmux. The sidebar turns on SGR mouse press/release reporting only (no motion, which 'floods stdin'), strips mouse sequences before Ink sees them and re-emits them as click events (click to highlight, double-click to open, v5.10.0). Popups are modal: all keys go to the popup process, Esc cancels, Enter submits. From inside any agent pane, Alt+Shift+M (a tmux key binding that runs `dmux --remote-pane-action`, queued to the sidebar and signalled with SIGUSR2) opens the pane menu over that pane.
input_model.note: [measured] src/utils/sidebarMouse.ts header comment, src/index.ts (remote pane action CLI, SIGUSR2 hook), commit 0fdf37e 'adds click-to-highlight, and double-click open sidebar'.

steal_for_td.value: Make a viewer a pane kind bound to the pane it came from, placed by a width policy instead of by halving. dmux's `f` opens a read-only file-browser pane rooted at the selected pane's worktree that stays in that pane's project group (code↔diff with d/Tab, Esc backs out), and every new pane goes through one layout calculator with comfortable bounds (sidebar 40, pane min 50 / max 80 columns, columns before rows). TD's Ctrl+click should open the Markdown/HTML/image viewer as a child of the source pane (inherits cwd, hides and closes with it) and ask the same kind of layout policy for its size, so an agent pane is never squeezed below a readable width.
steal_for_td.note: [inferred] Design recommendation drawn from core-concepts.js ('Browser panes stay associated with the same project group as their source worktree'), context/LAYOUT.md and src/constants/layout.ts. In gpui this is a pane variant in TD's split tree, not a tmux pane.

trap.value: Don't coordinate the UI from outside the thing that owns the panes. dmux drives tmux by shelling out, signals and temp files, and its tracker shows the cost: #101, a tmux `client-resized` hook sends SIGUSR1 to dmux, the listener lives in a React effect that unregisters on every dialog toggle, so a resize kills the control pane; the dead process leaves mouse reporting on (garbage like `73M64` typed into the shell) and hooks keep signalling a recycled PID. #111, popups pass ~2 KB of JSON in argv and endpoint-security software SIGKILLs the repeated execs. TD owns its panes in-process; keep viewers and floating squares as gpui elements with RAII teardown of mouse modes, not child processes talking through signals.
trap.note: [inferred] Lesson inferred from measured issue bodies #101 (open, 2026-07-28) and #111 (open, 2026-08-25).

what_it_is.value: The reference terminal multiplexer (server/client; sessions, windows, panes). For graphical content it has display-popup (modal floating overlay running a command, since 3.2), floating panes (3.7: non-modal panes above the tiled layout with full escape-sequence support; 3.8-rc adds modal panes, keyboard move/resize and float↔tile conversion), allow-passthrough so programs can tunnel raw escapes (Kitty/iTerm2 images) to the outer terminal, and built-in SIXEL when compiled with --enable-sixel (3.4). Kitty graphics are not in any release; PR #5445 is open.
what_it_is.note: [measured] CHANGES: 'Add basic support for SIXEL if built with --enable-sixel' (3.3a→3.4); 'Add floating panes…' (3.6b→3.7); 3.7c→3.8 floating/modal entries; 'Add support for per-client transient popups… display-popup' (3.1c→3.2).

language.value: C (2.92 MB), with Shell test scripts (0.78 MB), Roff man page, Yacc config grammar

graphics_mechanism.value: Draws no pixels itself. SIXEL (3.4+, --enable-sixel): tmux parses SIXEL from a pane, stores the image server-side (image.c, image-sixel.c) and re-sends it to each attached client that supports SIXEL, scaled and placed for that client; images are removed before reflow, saved/restored across the alternate screen (3.6), capped at 20 (3.6). Anything else only via allow-passthrough (`ESC P tmux; … ESC \` wrapping), which bypasses tmux's grid. Kitty graphics: unreleased — #4902 proof-of-concept branch ta/kitty-img, #5274 (Unicode-placeholder version, closed 2026-08-05), and open PR #5445 (mgrant0) which cuts Kitty and SIXEL images into cell-sized rectangles so they work around floating panes and scroll into copy mode.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] PR #5445 body, issue #4902 thread (nicm: 'When we get a SIXEL image, we store it… then when we need to redraw it we can… or replace it with a placeholder'), tree listing (image.c, image-sixel.c), CHANGES, tmux.1 allow-passthrough entry.

where_it_draws.value: split pane (tiled layout) + floating panel (display-popup modal overlay; 3.7 floating panes sit above tiled panes, cascaded from the top-left or placed with -X/-Y, sized with -x/-y in cells or %, -A keeps one above a zoomed pane) + inline in the pane grid for SIXEL (grid-resident, scrolls with the pane). Passthrough images are invisible to tmux's grid, so they neither clip to the pane nor scroll with it.
where_it_draws.note: [measured] new-pane entry in tmux.1 (lines ~3684-3725) and CHANGES. The passthrough-does-not-scroll point is [inferred] from #5274's description of the overlay approach ('clip to their pane, scroll with the text, and coexist — none of which the overlay approach could do').

input_model.value: display-popup is modal: keys go to the popup command until it exits (-E), -k lets any key dismiss (3.6), focus events are sent to the pane when entering/leaving a popup, and button-3 outside the border opens a menu to close or expand it. 3.7 floating panes are ordinary panes (focus by click, move/resize by mouse only). 3.8-rc: new-pane -O makes a modal pane (one per window, blocks other panes), -K sends every key including the prefix to it, -C closes it on a click outside; move-pane/resize-pane and new C-b g bindings move and resize floats from the keyboard.

trap.value: Image placements that aren't bound to pane visibility leak across panes. In 0.45.0 a yazi image preview stayed on screen after its stacked pane was hidden and showed through whatever pane was switched to (#5512); earlier, yazi images rendered in the wrong place unless the pane was fullscreen (#4101), partly because apps like Yazi hard-code Zellij env-var checks (PR #5428). Every TD image or viewer must follow its pane's visibility and geometry (hide, stack, zoom, tab switch) and be deleted with it.

what_it_is.value: Arcan is a display server and 'desktop engine': a Lua-scripted multimedia engine plus the SHMIF IPC and TUI API, which aims to replace terminal escape protocols altogether. Durden is its tiling/stacking desktop. Cat9 is a Lua user shell for Lash (Arcan's TUI command line) in which every command becomes a tracked job whose output can be folded, reused, popped out as a window or, through `open`, embedded as media (image, PDF, video) decoded by a separate afsrv_decode process into a clipped region of the shell's own window.
what_it_is.note: [measured] cat9 README ('It cooperates with your desktop window manager… letting it take care of splitting out things into new windows or even embedding media or graphical application output into clipped regions of its own window'), arcan README, durden README.

license.value: Mixed. arcan: GitHub reports NOASSERTION; COPYING lists 3-Clause BSD (engine, shmif, platform), GPLv2+ (arcan_lua.c 'as an artifical restriction'), LGPL (some frameservers). cat9: Unlicense. durden: BSD-3-Clause.

provenance.source: measured 2026-09-24: gh api repos/letoram/arcan, repos/letoram/cat9, repos/letoram/durden

language.value: cat9: Lua (100%). durden: Lua (+ GLSL). arcan: historically C + Lua, but the GitHub master now reports Zig 19.2 MB, Lua 0.88 MB, C 36 KB (435 .zig files; July 2026 commits port the compositor to Windows and macOS).
language.note: [measured] languages API for all three repos and a recursive tree count of arcan file extensions. The Zig figure is odd for Arcan; see gap-note bubble.

graphics_mechanism.value: Native display-server compositing, no escape-sequence graphics. cat9 `open` runs `file -b --mime-type`, maps image/* to proto=image, video/audio to proto=media, application/pdf to proto=pdf and text to proto=text, then hands the job to an afsrv_decode frameserver (a one-shot separate process) in a new window requested from the window manager; pixels travel over SHMIF shared memory. The 2017 design post lists 'Crazy encoding schemes for representing non-character data – such as Sixel' among the problems TUI replaces.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] open.lua (mime_direct / mime_prefix tables, phandover(… {"afsrv_decode"} …)); 2017 post read via WebFetch.

where_it_draws.value: Placement is a hint to the outer WM. cat9's dir_lut maps new→split, tnew/lnew/dnew/vnew→split-t/-l/-d, tab→tab, swallow→swallow (takes the place of the current window until closed) and embed→embed (anchored to a job inside the shell window; its resized/visibility handlers relayout and hide it with the job, and collapsed_rows reserves rows). Per the 2022 post the embedded resource 'scales, repositions and folds accordingly, yet the user can drag it out'. So: split, tab, floating (Durden) or a job-row-anchored embed that moves with the shell's layout.
where_it_draws.note: [measured] open.lua lines 1-160; cat9 README 'Term' prefixes (v/t/s/p); 2022 blog via WebFetch.

input_model.value: Input arrives as typed IPC events, not in-band bytes: 'Pasting is separated from entering text, is separated from pressing keys', and keyboard shortcuts are 'announced and semantically tagged, letting the graphical shell provide automation, rebinding'. In cat9, mouse clicks are keyed by region (titlebar, data body, line-number column) and behave like typed commands (bnd.m2_data_col_click = 'view #csel select $=crow'). Embedded media is its own window, so the WM routes focus to it; 'Detach and reattach embedded media, preserving input routing.'
input_model.note: [measured] Author's own blog (bjornstahl, 2022-04-02) and Lash#Cat9 post (2022-10-15), both read via WebFetch extraction; cat9 README bindings section read directly.

td_overlap.note: [inferred] pane-content (media embedded in the shell window), tui-wm (the shell drives window placement through the WM). Not host-protocol: it rejects escape-sequence graphics by design.

steal_for_td.value: One `open(target, placement)` verb with a MIME router and a small placement vocabulary. cat9 sniffs the type, picks a decoder, then asks for split / split-direction / tab / swallow / embed; swallow replaces the current window until closed and embed anchors the result to a row of the job that produced it, folding and hiding with it, while the user can still drag it out. TD's Ctrl+click, a `td open` CLI and any OSC request should all call one such function: `.md` → Markdown viewer, `.html` → web view, `image/*` → image view, with placement ∈ {split, vsplit, tab, float, swallow, embed-at-row}.
steal_for_td.note: [inferred] Mapped from open.lua dir_lut and mime tables onto TD's gpui split tree. 'embed-at-row' matches TD's floating-square-in-the-current-pane idea but anchors it to scrollback.

trap.value: Don't make the feature depend on programs adopting a new protocol. Arcan's embedding works because clients speak SHMIF/TUI instead of ECMA-48, and the price shows: cat9 says installing is 'not for the faint of heart', legacy tty programs need a `!`/`p!` escape into a terminal emulator, and the project has stayed niche (cat9 526 stars; GitHub mirror 'going defunct'). TD should get Ctrl+click opening entirely from its own side (path/URL detection, OSC 8) and accept the protocols programs already emit (Kitty, Sixel) for pixels.
trap.note: [inferred] From the cat9 README installation section and 'Term' prefixes plus measured star counts.

what_it_is.value: Rust 'terminal workspace manager' and background server that keeps agent and shell panes running across detach (workspaces → tabs → panes), marks every agent pane working / blocked / idle / done, exposes a CLI and socket API that agents themselves drive, and supports manifest plugins with panes and Ctrl-click link handlers. It runs inside any host terminal and since 0.9.0 shows pane images by re-emitting Kitty graphics to compatible hosts. Omarchy v4.0.4 installs it (omarchy-base.packages line 52) and binds it to Super+Ctrl+Return.

graphics_mechanism.value: Kitty graphics protocol, re-emitted. libghostty-vt parses each pane's stream, Kitty images included (herdr caps image storage at 64 MiB and supplies a PNG-decode callback); the client composes placements per surface with visibility states Main / Popup / Hidden and an occlusion map, then writes Kitty APCs to the host. Direct file transfer (t=t) is used only after a silent 1x1 query proves the local Ghostty consumes it (src/client/image_files.rs). On by default since 0.9.0 (`terminal.kitty_graphics = false` to disable); Unicode placeholders render (#136).

where_it_draws.value: split panes and tabs (tiled), zoomed, a session-modal floating popup (placement = popup: half-size by default, or cell / % sizes) and an overlay (placement = overlay: a temporary zoomed overlay over the active pane that restores the previous focus and zoom on close). Images are cell-anchored placements inside a pane and follow its scroll; since 0.9.1 popups and notifications hide only the image placements they overlap.

updates.label: dmux-rs — native Rust tmux control-mode renderer for dmux

what_it_is.value: Standard Agents' Rust rewrite of dmux's front end. Instead of an Ink sidebar driving tmux by shelling out, it attaches as a tmux control-mode client, keeps its own VT grid per pane (alacritty_terminal 0.25), composites the panes plus a native overlay UI (sidebar, menus, settings, diff pager, toasts) and paints the host terminal itself. It ships as a 'first-party test ring' that self-updates every minute and auto-files rendering-divergence issues.

language.value: Rust (1.29 MB) + Shell (98 KB). Workspace crates: dmux-cc (control-mode client), dmux-vt (alacritty_terminal 0.25), dmux-compositor, dmux-host, dmux-ui, dmux-status, dmux-infer; also termwiz 0.23 and crossterm 0.29.

graphics_mechanism.value: Host-terminal cells, plus Kitty graphics for its own chrome only: crates/dmux-host/src/kitty.rs is a 'Stateful Kitty graphics encoder for small direct-RGBA overlays' (upload once per asset key, move placements by reusing image/placement ids so Kitty replaces them without flicker; an 'experiment/kitty-accent-cursor-motion' branch merged 2026-08-25). Program images inside panes are not passed through: ROADMAP lists 'Images (kitty graphics translation) ⏳'.

where_it_draws.value: Composited split panes (following the tmux layout) plus native overlays drawn by dmux-rs in the same host terminal: sidebar, pane menu, confirm and input dialogs, settings, diff pager, toasts, and title-bar click buttons ('not possible under tmux'). Pane text scrolls as that pane's VT grid.
where_it_draws.note: [measured] ROADMAP 'Popups → native overlays' inventory and 'Title-bar click affordances'.

input_model.value: ROADMAP's 'toes' policy: leader Ctrl+b (Ctrl+b Ctrl+b sends a literal), a one-key overlay cheat-sheet on leader; Super/Cmd globals only when the host speaks the kitty keyboard protocol (probed at startup), since those keys never reach pane apps; only Ctrl+q and Ctrl+y as bare chords; overlays swallow all input while open and Esc closes them; kitty keyboard flags forwarded into panes that push them; drag-select with OSC 52 copy.

activity.value: 0 stars · created 2026-08-19 · pushed 2026-08-30 · latest release v0.38.0 (2026-08-30)
activity.note: [measured] Public repo; the README's installer expects `gh` access to the repo.

td_overlap.note: [inferred] same-stack (Rust + alacritty_terminal 0.25, TD's own VT engine), agent-panes, tui-wm, floating (native overlays), host-protocol (emits Kitty graphics and uses kitty keyboard on the host).

steal_for_td.value: Copy the shadow verifier. dmux-rs runs a second, independent VT parser over the same byte stream (tmux's grid), compares every settled pane cell-for-cell against its alacritty_terminal grid, and on a mismatch writes an incident with both grids plus a seed-anchored raw byte recording; `--replay-incident` reproduces it offline and fixed incidents go into a corpus replayed in CI forever. TD should do the same before adding Kitty/Sixel and viewer placements on top of alacritty_terminal: record pane bytes, replay them into a reference parser, and lock every divergence into a test corpus.
steal_for_td.note: [inferred] From ROADMAP 'Rendering-fidelity contract'. A candidate oracle for TD is libghostty-vt (see herdr), which also parses Kitty graphics.

trap.value: Picking alacritty_terminal leaves graphics to you: dmux-rs, on the same engine, still lists pane images as '⏳ later', and upstream Alacritty's maintainer said on 2026-07-07 that Alacritty should not implement Sixel because 'Many of the usecases you've listed are things I never want to see in my terminal'. Don't plan TD's Kitty/Sixel support as waiting for alacritty_terminal; budget a TD-owned graphics parser and image store beside the grid from the start.
trap.note: [inferred] Combines the measured ROADMAP status with the measured maintainer comment (chrisduerr) on alacritty#910. Whether alacritty_terminal's parser exposes APC/DCS hooks TD can tap was not checked this session.

primary_sources.note: [measured] Read via gh api on 2026-09-24. Subject suggested by a sibling gatherer and verified independently.

updates.label: cmux — Ghostty-based agent terminal with Markdown and browser panes

what_it_is.value: Native macOS terminal app (Swift/AppKit; terminal rendering via libghostty) built for running many coding agents. It has a vertical-tab sidebar with branch, PR, ports and notification text, notification rings on panes that need attention, and non-terminal panes beside terminals: a WKWebView browser pane, a live-reloading Markdown viewer and File Preview panels, opened by Cmd-click on paths and links or by `cmux markdown open plan.md` / `cmux open`.

license.value: GPL-3.0-or-later (LICENSE file; GitHub reports NOASSERTION because of a commercial-terms preamble)
license.note: [measured] spdx NOASSERTION; LICENSE text: 'licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later (GPL-3.0-or-later)'.

language.value: Swift (87.6 MB) dominant; also Rust 18.7 MB, TypeScript 13.2 MB, Python 10.3 MB, Zig 1.2 MB (libghostty)

graphics_mechanism.value: Native GPU terminal via libghostty ('the same way apps use WebKit for web views') plus embedded web views: the Markdown viewer was 'Rewritten… with a webview-based renderer' (#3664; Resources/markdown-viewer/shell.html; tables, Mermaid, inline images), and browser panes are WKWebView (Sources/Panels/WKWebView+*.swift) with a scriptable agent-browser API. Whether terminal panes accept Kitty graphics from programs was not verified.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] CHANGELOG (#3664), README ('Powered by libghostty'), gh code search hits for WKWebView under Sources/Panels.

where_it_draws.value: split pane: `cmux markdown open` 'opens as a horizontal split to the right of the source surface'; Cmd+Shift+L opens a browser in a split; panels are tabs in the split tree and are restored across sessions (the Markdown panel re-reads the file from disk and is not recreated if the file is gone). Not inline in scrollback; no separate OS window.

input_model.value: Cmd-click on terminal text routes by type: Markdown paths → Markdown viewer (#4864; first an opt-in setting, #2904), HTML files → browser pane (#9096), other supported files → cmux (#4041), URLs → the built-in browser, including inside fullscreen TUIs like Claude Code and Codex (#5406) and OSC 8 links (#3580). Viewer and browser panes take native AppKit focus (Cmd+F find, zoom). Everything is scriptable over the CLI and a Unix socket.
input_model.note: [measured] CHANGELOG entries cited by PR number.

td_overlap.note: [inferred] The closest shipped match to TD's feature: Cmd-click a .md/.html path → viewer pane beside the terminal. Not same-stack (Swift + libghostty), no floating squares found.

steal_for_td.value: Ship the viewer as a live-reloading pane that agents can open, not only people. `cmux markdown open plan.md` splits a Markdown panel to the right, re-renders on every write (atomic saves handled), and cmux tells agents in AGENTS.md to write the whole plan first and then open it. TD should expose the same route as Ctrl+click through a `td open <path>` CLI (or OSC request) with file watching, so an agent's plan, brief or HTML report appears beside its pane and stays current.
steal_for_td.note: [inferred] From SKILL.md ('Write the full plan file first, then open it, so the panel never shows a partially written file'). Fits Parker's existing 'Deliverable:' line convention, which already names the file an agent wants opened.

trap.value: Click-to-open detection is where the bugs live. cmux's changelog shows Markdown paths with trailing punctuation detected as URLs (#4594), Cmd-click failing on soft-wrapped URLs (#8110), clicks swallowed inside fullscreen TUIs that capture the mouse (#5406), OSC 8 Cmd-click broken (#3580), a recursive-lock crash on the Markdown route (#3559), and blank Markdown viewers after resize or being dragged to another column (#10474, #6331). TD should match paths on the logical (unwrapped) line with punctuation trimming, honour Ctrl+click even when the app has mouse reporting on, and keep viewer state alive across re-parenting.

primary_sources.note: [measured] Read via gh api on 2026-09-24. cmux is a terminal app, so cluster A may also claim it.

updates.label: Claude Squad — agent sessions on tmux + worktrees

what_it_is.value: Go TUI (`cs`) that manages several terminal agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Aider, …), each in its own tmux session and git worktree: an instance list on the left, a live preview tab and a diff tab on the right, Enter to attach full-screen, commit/push and pause/resume per instance. Text only.
what_it_is.note: [measured] README 'How It Works': tmux sessions, git worktrees, 'A simple TUI interface'.

language.value: Go (263 KB): bubbletea v1.3.4, lipgloss, creack/pty

graphics_mechanism.value: none — text cells only. The preview tab is `tmux capture-pane -p -e -J` output (ANSI kept, wrapped lines joined) re-rendered inside a lipgloss box; status detection re-captures the pane and compares content / looks for prompts (HasUpdated).

where_it_draws.value: split inside its own TUI (list | tabbed preview/diff window); attaching replaces the whole terminal with `tmux attach-session` through a PTY (fullscreen) until Ctrl-q.
where_it_draws.note: [measured] tmux.go Attach/Restore (exec tmux attach-session via ptyFactory), README menu.

input_model.value: Bubbletea key handling: n / N new (with prompt), ↑/↓ or j/k select, Tab switches preview↔diff, shift-↑/↓ scrolls the diff, Enter/o attaches (keys then go straight to the agent through the attached PTY), Ctrl-q detaches back to the list.

td_overlap.note: [inferred] Agent multiplexer on tmux + worktrees; no floating, no graphics.

steal_for_td.value: A read-only peek: selecting an agent in the list shows its live screen in a side panel without moving focus, and Tab flips the same panel to that worktree's diff; Enter commits to a full attach. TD can offer this as a floating square: hover or select a pane in the sidebar to peek at its live grid, Tab for its git diff, Enter to focus. The floating square then shows other panes as well as files.

trap.value: Don't build the peek from re-captured text. claude-squad polls `capture-pane` and re-renders the ANSI inside lipgloss, which drops anything that isn't cells (no images), costs a subprocess per refresh, and has mangled wide characters (#233, 'Chinese/Unicode characters display as garbled text'). TD holds every pane's alacritty_terminal grid in-process, so a peek should render that grid (and its image placements) directly.
trap.note: [inferred] From tmux.go capture path and issue #233 title (closed); root cause of #233 not read.

what_it_is.value: A text-mode windowing environment that 'implements in text mode the same concepts that X11 does in graphics': overlapping, draggable, resizable windows with per-window menus and gadgets, virtual screens, a built-in window manager and truecolor terminal emulator, networked clients (libtw) and displays that attach and detach on the fly (twdisplay). Runs on the Linux console, in X11, in a tty, or nested in itself.

license.value: GPL-2.0 (server and clients); libtutf and libtw are LGPL
license.note: [measured] spdx GPL-2.0; README 'COPYING.LIB' note for the libraries.

graphics_mechanism.value: none — text cells only. Under X11 twin opens its own window and draws the cell grid (Xft build dependency); no image protocol appears in README or Tutorial.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] README display list and build deps; absence of image support is [inferred] from README/Tutorial greps, not a source audit.

where_it_draws.value: floating (overlapping) windows in a cell grid with raise/lower stacking and maximize; virtual screens up to ~64K cells, scrolled by dragging to the screen edge; window contents may exceed the window and scroll.

input_model.value: The built-in WM 'does window focus changes, window drags and resizes, virtual screen changes, menu activity and dispatches keystrokes and mouse events to the focused window'. PAUSE or the right mouse button opens the focused window's menu; its Window item offers Move, Resize, Scroll, Center, Maximize, Raise/Lower and a Window List. On generic ttys the mouse works only with xterm-style reporting.
input_model.note: [measured] Tutorial sections 1-2 and the menu walkthrough (~lines 270-321).

activity.note: [measured] repo metadata and releases/latest (README header still says 0.9.1).

td_overlap.note: [inferred] Overlapping draggable windows inside a text environment; no graphics, no agents.

steal_for_td.value: Make floating squares fully keyboard-operable and listable, not mouse-only. twin puts Move, Resize, Center, Maximize, Raise/Lower on every window's menu and keeps a Window List that focuses and centres the chosen window. TD's draggable square should likewise have a keyboard move/resize mode, snap-to-centre / maximize-within-pane, and a list of open squares; tmux 3.7 shipped floating panes mouse-only and had to add keyboard move/resize in 3.8.
steal_for_td.note: [inferred] From twin's Tutorial menu section and tmux CHANGES 3.7/3.8.

trap.value: A window manager built out of cells inherits cell limits: twin windows can hold only text, geometry snaps to the character grid, and on generic ttys mouse handling depends on the host's reporting ('it may have problems with mouse (only xterm and derivatives have a standard to report mouse)'). TD's floating square should be a gpui layer with pixel geometry and native input, placed over the terminal grid, not a window emulated inside it.

bubbles.note: Boyd (@0xBOYD) is Andrew Boyd, 'Founder @standardagents. AgentBuilder, dmux, formkit', and dmux.ai credits him beside Justin Schroeder (@jpschroeder). The Jev-plays-Pokemon post and dmux come from the same people.
bubbles.why: Cluster E can connect Boyd's dashboard to dmux / dmux-rs. Parker named both, so they are probably one lineage.

bubbles.note: Alacritty's maintainer (chrisduerr, 2026-07-07) on alacritty#910: Alacritty should not implement Sixel, 'Many of the usecases you've listed are things I never want to see in my terminal'. Zellij's maintainer cited this as 'the last straw' for adding Kitty graphics to Zellij (PR #5428).
bubbles.why: TD's VT engine is alacritty_terminal, so upstream will not add image parsing. TD owns graphics parsing and the image store, or swaps/augments the engine.

bubbles.note: herdr drives a vendored libghostty-vt from Rust over its C ABI as its per-pane VT engine, and that engine already parses Kitty graphics (herdr sets a 64 MiB image storage limit and a PNG decode callback). cmux uses libghostty too.
bubbles.why: A proven Rust-reachable VT engine with Kitty graphics built in, usable as TD's graphics path or as the independent oracle for a dmux-rs-style shadow verifier against alacritty_terminal.

bubbles.note: dmux's PaneAnalyzer is an LLM prompt-and-parse step over the last 50 lines of a pane: state ∈ {option_dialog, open_prompt, in_progress}, the options with keys, potentialHarm {hasRisk, description}, a summary, with a 5 s content-hash cache. Cheap regex heuristics (spinner glyphs, prompt patterns, progress words) run first and the LLM is the escalation. PR #88 (closed) tried a 45 s 'task adherence' LLM check.
bubbles.why: This is exactly the typed judgment TypeSafe/Jev is for: a Choice over the three states plus a Noul for 'this option is risky', batched over one pane state. A TD attention rail could do it on the in-process grid with no capture-pane.

bubbles.note: dmux deleted its HTTP API, SSE stream, Vue web dashboard and tunnel/QR remote on 2026-02-20 (commit 75cd109) and stayed tmux + TUI only, and dmux-rs marks 'web/remote ✂' (dropped). Meanwhile agent-deck ships `agent-deck web` (127.0.0.1:8420) and zellij added a web client with PWA and mobile UI in 0.45.
bubbles.why: The agent-multiplexer field is split on browser surfaces. Standard Agents dropped theirs, which is evidence for keeping TD's rich content inside the terminal window rather than beside it in a browser.

bubbles.note: tmux PR #5445 introduces a per-terminal 'imagescroll' feature after direct testing: only WezTerm and Ghostty are confirmed to move SIXEL/Kitty image content with a scrolled region (mintty scrolls text in margins but drops the image); everything else gets an explicit redraw after scroll.
bubbles.why: Cluster B can use this capability matrix, and TD should know it if it ever re-emits images to a host (e.g. TD inside SSH or a nested terminal).

bubbles.note: tmux itself is converging on TD's floating-square idea: 3.7 (2026-06-26) added non-modal floating panes; 3.8-rc (2026-09-09) adds modal panes (-O, -K, -C), float↔tile via break-pane/join-pane, keyboard move/resize, and JSON layout strings that include floating panes.
bubbles.why: Users of TD agent panes running tmux inside will soon have floats inside floats; TD's own floating layer should not fight tmux's for the mouse.

bubbles.note: cmux has a skill (skills/cmux-markdown) telling agents to write plan.md and run `cmux markdown open plan.md` so the plan appears in a live-reloading split beside the agent.
bubbles.why: Direct precedent for letting agents, not only humans, open TD viewers, and it fits Parker's 'Deliverable:' line convention, which already names the one file an agent wants opened.

bubbles.note: Zellij's plugin API has an 'in place' placement family (open_file_in_place, open_terminal_in_place, open_command_pane_in_place: 'temporarily replacing the focused pane'); herdr's overlay placement does the same with zoom and restores focus and zoom on close; cat9 calls it 'swallow'.
bubbles.why: Three independent projects converge on a third placement beyond split and float, which TD's open-on-click should offer.

bubbles.note: Other agent multiplexers checked, not added as subjects: asheshgoplani/agent-deck (MIT, 947 stars, v1.16.16 2026-09-20; tmux-based, web UI on 127.0.0.1:8420, phone-driven 'conductor', MCP manager); stravu/crystal, renamed Nimbalyst (MIT, 3.1k stars, desktop app, last push 2026-02-26); devflowinc/uzi (MIT, 582 stars, dormant since 2025-06-04).
bubbles.why: Candidate subjects if the survey widens the agent-multiplexer set; agent-deck is the most active.

bubbles.note: Candidate for cluster D: lnqs/textual-image (LGPL-3.0, 183 stars, v0.13.1 2026-05-29, pushed 2026-09-24) renders images in Textual/rich apps. Textualize/textual (MIT, 37.3k stars, v8.2.8) and textual-web (MIT, 1.5k stars, last release 2024-02-20) run TUIs in a browser.
bubbles.why: Textual is the Python counterpart of ratatui for widget-level image placement; not added to cluster C because it is a framework rather than a multiplexer or window manager.
